example_prompt: Check whether an Intron text-to-speech job is done and get the generated audio's location.

text_id.description: the text id generated in response when the text was queued. Passed as a path parameter.

audio_path.description: Location of the generated audio (documented example: "http://myaudio.wav"). Lifetime and download auth are not documented.

processing_status.description: Values listed on the Get Text Status page.

status.description: "Ok" in the documented examples, including the 503 timeout body.

gotchas: The API key comes from the developers tab of your account on voice.intron.io; send it as 'Authorization: Bearer {key}' from your backend only — the docs say never expose it in client-side code.

Poll until processing_status is TTS_TEXT_AUDIO_GENERATED or TTS_TEXT_AUDIO_PROCESSING_FAILED (other values: TTS_TEXT_AUDIO_QUEUED, TTS_TEXT_AUDIO_PENDING, TTS_TEXT_AUDIO_PROCESSING). The documented in-progress example already contains audio_path and audio_duration_in_seconds — only use audio_path once the status is TTS_TEXT_AUDIO_GENERATED.
The response does not echo text_id — keep it on your side.
audio_path is the generated audio's location (example "http://myaudio.wav"). How long it stays valid and whether downloading it needs the API key are not documented — download it promptly.
No error response is documented for this endpoint (unknown text_id, invalid key, rate limit).
Rate limit: 100 requests per minute on tts/v1/status. Responses carry rate-limit headers; Retry-After gives the delay in seconds before retrying.

spans: the text id generated in response when the text was queued
